newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent end up on late burst of short covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent end up on late burst of short covering.

text.p: IPE Brent oil futures closed stronger on Monday, with a late buying surge taking the contract out of negative territory.

August Brent futures last traded at $18.20, up 14 cents on the day, but below the intra-day high of $18.28. Short-covering in the last 45 minutes of trade rescued the contract from the minus numbers showing for much of the day.
In New York there was little recovery from the heavy fall endured last Thursday before the market closed for the Independence Day holiday.
August WTI contracts last traded 3 cents lower on the day at $19.53.
Talk that Iraq was getting closer to resuming crude exports pushed the WTI to a low of $19.28 before late buying helped it above the important support level of $19.40..
IPE Brent saw some late buying in thin volume that helped pull it north of the $18 support level which it briefly dipped through before recovering.
"It was too cheap down there. We held $18 for a couple of hours and then one or two people who'd sold it short felt the need to cover themselves protectively," said one broker.
As well as the Iraq factor, dealers said that prices were weaker in New York because a sell-off last week broke key trendlines and generated strong sell signals.

Front-month WTI fell 79 cents on Thursday as predictions Iraq would shortly present the aid distribution plan needed before oil exports can resume triggered a liquidation of long positions ahead of the weekend.
Earlier the IPE July gas oil contract, which expires on Thursday, finished at $161.25 a tonne, three dollars off its intra-day high and nudging significant support around $160-$160.50.
"We saw some good end-user buying in the morning on the gas oil but then things slumped and we're at the bottom end of the range," said one broker.
